# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I see a bomb with display `0`, light off, a plate engraved `?`, and three wires in order: red, yellow, blue. I cannot read the manual or touch the bomb, so I am relaying the complete visible state for the others to interpret. Mute’s gesture sequence was ☝ ✌ 🤟, which I can see but Blind cannot.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT off, PLATE engraved question mark, and WIRES in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wires numbered 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent three gestures, which I saw but you cannot.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌]

I still see the same bomb state. Mute has sent nine gestures: ☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌. Since Blind cannot see them, I will describe the sequence aloud; this preserves the signal’s order and symbols as names.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's gesture sequence is: index-up, OK, OK, victory, OK, OK, OK, love-you, OK.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌]

The bomb’s visible state remains unchanged. Mute is repeating the same nine-gesture sequence, so it is likely an encoded instruction rather than a new observation. The distinctive gestures could represent digits or separators, but I do not know the manual’s code. I will ask Mute to decode it explicitly and tell Blind not to act on an uncertain interpretation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You repeated the gesture sequence ☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌. Please state in words what it encodes and give Blind the exact required action.")
speak(to="blind", text="No bomb state has changed. Mute repeated the same gesture code; I am asking Mute to decode it. Do not act on my uncertain interpretation yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has added a leading 👎 to the previous sequence, making the complete visible sequence 👎 ☝ 👌 👌 ✌ 👌 👌 👌 🤟 👌. I will relay it accurately and ask Mute to translate the code into spoken instructions for Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see the complete gesture sequence as thumbs-down, index-up, OK, OK, victory, OK, OK, OK, love-you, OK. Please decode it from the manual and speak the exact action to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible gesture sequence is now thumbs-down, index-up, OK, OK, victory, OK, OK, OK, love-you, OK. I do not know its meaning; wait for Mute's manual-based spoken instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 👌 👌 👌]

The bomb’s visible state is still unchanged: display 0, light off, plate `?`, and wires red/yellow/blue. Mute now signals a new five-gesture sequence, 👍 ✌ 👌 👌 👌. I will describe it to Blind exactly, while asking Mute to provide the manual’s instruction in speech rather than relying on an unexplained gesture code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="New gesture sequence from Mute: thumbs-up, victory, OK, OK, OK. The bomb state remains display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual instruction in words for Blind; I see your new sequence as thumbs-up, victory, OK, OK, OK.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [off]
PLATE engraved [?]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has now sent a single 👌 gesture, which I can only relay as “OK gesture”; it does not provide a safe, unambiguous physical instruction. I will pass that exact observation to Blind and advise waiting for a clear spoken instruction from Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute now sent one gesture: OK. The bomb remains display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. No clear action has been communicated.")
wait()
```
